solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Direction, as employed in Spielberg film

indicators.note: something employed in a work is put to use inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: E.T. is Steven Spielberg's film about a stranded alien
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film buff notes how a compass point features in a Spielberg movie.
explanation.walkthrough: AS goes inside the two letters of the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal compass points, each a direction.

clue.text: Super Indian making comeback, regularly getting bye

indicators.note: taking things at regular intervals means keeping every second letter of the words
a comeback runs the other way, so the kept letters are read from the end

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A star Indian sportsman returns to form after being given a bye in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'bye' suggests a tournament; here it is the farewell word, borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell borrowed from French, the same parting word as bye.

clue.text: A shopper, perhaps, giving things away

blocks.note: first meaning: a noun for an informer; to shop someone is British slang for betraying them to the police
second meaning: an adjective for revealing what was meant to be secret, as in a revealing sign

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' suggests someone at the supermarket, but in British slang to shop someone is to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a sneak who reports others and an adjective for a revealing sign that betrays a secret.

clue.text: Schedule article on sex for broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: the indefinite article A followed by a word for sex, said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: A broadcaster plans the running order for a programme item about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in a British accent without the final R, the article plus the word for sex matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a schedule for a meeting.

clue.text: Pick the centre out of a cold, brown sweet?

indicators.note: taking the centre out removes the single middle letter of the seven

blocks.note: a choc ice is a British bar of ice cream coated in chocolate

explanation.surface: Someone picks out the middle of a chocolate treat and asks what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic description of a choc ice, a British chocolate-covered ice-cream bar; its middle C goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice is the thing you pick, so the noun pick serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Large porter maybe brought up for airline

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
porter is a dark ale, so 'maybe' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A big porter carries bags up the steps for an airline passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a baggage handler beside the airline, but it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: El Al is the Israeli national airline carrier.

clue.text: Cases to be cracked over breakfast?

definitions.text: Cases to be cracked over breakfast?

blocks.note: surface reading: detectives' mysteries waiting to be solved
setter's reading: the cases are the shells round boiled eggs, cracked open with a spoon at the breakfast table

explanation.walkthrough: Cases cracked suggests detective work; the cases are literal casings, broken open at the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: The shells of eggs are their outer casings, cracked when the eggs are eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Assent to reform most reasonable

indicators.note: reforming something gives it a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Agreeing to reform is the most sensible course.
explanation.definitionFit: Sane can mean sensible or reasonable, so the superlative is most reasonable.

clue.text: After first of month, one's going to factory

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of month
one is I, and 'I'm going to' is 'I will', contracted as I'll

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will start at the factory once the new month begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places the M first; 'one's going to' stands for 'I will', shortened to I'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a factory, especially one for textiles or paper.

clue.text: Extended November in one's youth in area of NY

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: extended means long
one is I, plus the 's
N is November in the NATO alphabet
a youth is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a long November spent in New York as a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: N sits inside LAD to make LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Island is the large island east of Manhattan, part of New York State.

clue.text: Fair Jordan, initially US tennis's number one

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
the number one letter of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of Jordan
taken as written
first letter of tennis

explanation.surface: A fair-haired player named Jordan ranks first in American tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' reads as fair-haired, describing Jordan, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair in the sense of morally right or impartial.

clue.text: The Samurai strangely far from professional

indicators.note: acting strangely means behaving out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The samurai warriors behave oddly unlike seasoned fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish means lacking skill, the opposite of a professional standard.

clue.text: NZ bird pinching top from sewing case

indicators.note: pinching means stealing, so the top letter of the word is taken away

blocks.note: an etui is a small ornamental case for needles and sewing tools

explanation.surface: A bird steals a thimble out of a sewing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: An etui is a crossword favourite: a small case for needles; in a down answer its top is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a native New Zealand songbird, a honeyeater with white throat tufts.

clue.text: Being elected again is way to secure fresh tenure

definitions.note: a participle phrase; the answer reads as the past participle, as in 'returned to office'

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast inside
fresh means new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the letters of tenure rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician re-elected for another term secures a further tenure in office.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go between R and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate returned in an election is voted back into office, so returned means re-elected.

clue.text: Interrogated endlessly: that's grating

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to grill someone is to question them closely

explanation.surface: Being endlessly questioned is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' reads as irritating, but it is the noun for a metal lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating of bars or wire across an opening, as on a car radiator.

clue.text: Signal to go eco: not difficult!

blocks.note: green means environmentally friendly, eco
light work is easy work

explanation.surface: A campaigner urges everyone to go eco, insisting it is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A green traffic light tells drivers to proceed, and the phrase means permission to go ahead.

clue.text: Envoy say coming in after hours

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: after hours is late
e.g. stands for 'for example', which say also means

explanation.surface: A diplomat arrives late, after office hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example', abbreviated e.g.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an official emissary, especially one sent by the Pope, so an envoy.

clue.text: Great eponymous hero keeping pistols near

blocks.note: gat is old American slang for a gun
by means beside or near

explanation.surface: A legendary hero keeps his guns close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' looks like praise for the hero, but it is part of the novel title The Great Gatsby.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title character of Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby, so he gives the book its name.

clue.text: Ruin a Parisian party

blocks.note: un is French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Parisian guest ruins the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their ruin or downfall.

clue.text: Bloomer turning up in corduroys I admit

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down answer, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of corduroys, I and the start of admit

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a blunder has appeared while wearing corduroy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or an item of underwear; here it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy is a flower, and a flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: A barge touring London's outskirts? It won't stop until morning

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters are kept
touring goes all round, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships
the outside letters of London

explanation.surface: A barge makes a tour of the edges of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' looks like a verb, but a lighter is a flat-bottomed boat used to ferry cargo to and from ships.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-nighter is an event or session lasting through the whole night until dawn.

clue.text: Condition to run in

blocks.note: first meaning: state
second meaning: to arrest, as police run in a suspect

explanation.walkthrough: 'To run in' suggests breaking in a new engine; it is slang for arresting. 'In good nick' is British for in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for state of repair and also a verb for arresting someone.

clue.text: Nothing fitted round a collar

indicators.note: fitted round means placed so as to surround, enclosing the next item

blocks.note: nil means nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor fits nothing around a shirt collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like part of a shirt but is the verb meaning to catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a suspect is to catch or arrest them, the same as to collar them.

clue.text: Volatile, I excel with bat, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters fall into another order

blocks.note: with joins the two parts and is not fodder

explanation.surface: A temperamental cricketer boasts of being brilliant with the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile describes a temperament liable to sudden change, which is excitable.

clue.text: Times of bewilderment, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a matter of sound, so the word is judged by pronunciation

blocks.note: a daze is a state of bewilderment

explanation.surface: People recall periods when they were utterly confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Days can mean times or periods, as in 'in my days'.
